D07_25.owns: Statement-level accounting anomaly and forensic red-flag detection from PIT financial-statement vintages.
primitivesConsumed: accounting-policy/estimate change context from sibling modules
doesNotOwn: audit opinion as an independent governance event
D07_25.decisionRole: Forensic risk/context flag and hypothesis generator; not proof of fraud/manipulation and not an automatic directional stock vote.

D21_10.decisionRole: Governance/control-process evidence, not a duplicate financial-ratio anomaly score.

sources: MOPS filed financial statements and XBRL instances
MOPS related-party and other statement-supporting disclosures where relevant
statementLane.clock: financialStatementFirstObservedAt / filing or publication timestamp where proven
statementLane.versioning: append-only statement vintage; correction/restatement creates a new vintage

sources: MOPS CPA internal-control special review report
MOPS/TWSE material information for restatement, modified audit opinion or internal-control statement change

sharedEvidenceReceipt.rule: One canonical source event/statement receipt may be referenced by both modules, but it creates no duplicate vote.

childViews.D07_25: Measures statement deltas/anomaly state before/after the event.
childViews.D21_10: Measures audit/control/governance event state and remediation.

divergentStateExamples.example: Receivables and inventory grow materially faster than sales while operating cash conversion deteriorates, but the filed audit opinion remains unmodified and no internal-control/restatement event is disclosed.
divergentStateExamples.interpretation: Statement anomaly exists without a governance/control event.

divergentStateExamples.example: An internal-control statement is amended or a CPA/control-process disclosure identifies a material control problem, while ordinary forensic ratios remain within prior ranges and no unusual cash/receivable/inventory divergence is observed.
divergentStateExamples.interpretation: Governance/control warning exists without a statement-ratio anomaly.

competingMechanismsAndFalsifiers: High accruals can reflect growth, working-capital investment or accounting reliability differences rather than manipulation.
Receivables/inventory growth can be rational during rapid demand expansion or supply-chain buffering.
Cash-flow weakness can arise from seasonal working-capital build, acquisitions or expansion.
Modified audit/control events can arise from scope, evidence or process deficiencies without proving intentional earnings manipulation.
A later restatement does not prove an earlier forensic metric could identify it ex ante.

If D07-25 adds no information beyond D07-07 earnings quality, D07-24 accounting-policy quality and existing statement primitives, narrow D07-25 to cross-signal forensic orchestration rather than a second score.
Financial institutions require separate anomaly semantics; industrial working-capital ratios must not be forced onto banks/insurers.
academicCounterevidence: Accrual components can be less persistent than cash components, but literature offers competing explanations including growth/investment, risk and measurement error.
Discretionary-accrual models can mismeasure normal accruals; abnormal accruals are not direct proof of manipulation.
Post-loss accrual/earnings behavior can reflect genuine operating recovery rather than window dressing.
antiDoubleCount: Raw accrual metric remains owned by D07-07; D07-25 may consume it only as one forensic primitive.
Accounting-policy change semantics remain owned by D07-24; D07-25 may consume only anomaly implications.
Restatement/audit/internal-control event is recorded once and linked to D07-25 and D21-10 child interpretations.
No combined System score may count the same restatement event once as forensic evidence and again as independent governance evidence without residualization.
specialistRecommendation: KEEP_SEPARATE if Room 14 confirms independent governance/control observables and child-event semantics; otherwise apply SCOPE_DEDUP_ONLY to any shared restatement/audit content.
